NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are

  site and a recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP -TV
  Channel 35 (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome on any item during City Council consideration of the item. An opportunity is
  also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If you would like to
  address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public comment, please
  complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MAY 27, 2025

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR STEGURA called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Kayla Groenleer, president of Peninsula High School’s Kick Ash.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff (7:09 pm), Schmitz, Stegura

City Council Members Absent:  Zerunyan

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Assistant City Attorney Steve McEwen
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton
  Administrative Services Director Michael Whitehead
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Assistant to the City Manager Jessica Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MAY 31, 2025 “WORLD NO TOBACCO DAY”

MAYOR STEGURA presented a proclamation to Kayla Groenleer, president of Peninsula
High School’s Kick Ash, declaring May 31, 2025 as “World No Tobacco Day.”

B.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING JUNE 2025 “LGBTQIA+ PRIDE MONTH”

MAYOR STEGURA presented a proclamation declaring June 2025 as LGBTQIA+ Pride
Month.

C.  RECOGNITION OF PUBLIC WORKS DIRECTOR DAVID WAHBA ON HIS
  RETIREMENT

MAYOR STEGURA presented a Resolution of Commendation to retiring Public Works
Director David Wahba, in honor of his 35 years of service to the City of Rolling Hills Estates.
She also presented Director Wahba with a gift, a Rolling Hills Estates Street sign titled
“Wahba Way.” Director Wahba thanked the Council, staff and City, and said a few words
about his many years with the City. Each Council Member spoke, commending Director
Wahba for his years of service, including Mayor Pro Tem Zerunyan as well as City Attorney
Donald Davis via pre-recorded video. Lastly City Manager Grammer said a few parting
words.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-G AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
MAY 27, 2025
 B.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  APPROVED.

C.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF MAY 2025

  APPROVED WARRANTS 68505 THROUGH 68530 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $257,568.65 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 050425 THROUGH
  050625 IN THE AMOUNT OF $133,099.71 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT
  OF $390,668.36 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

D.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF APRIL 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF APRIL 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  BUDGET AMENDMENTS FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025

  APPROVED THE BUDGET AMENDMENTS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-25.

G.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF MAY 13, 2025

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

H.  PALOS VERDES PENINSULA PUBLIC SAFETY COMMITTEE AND REGIONAL
  CONTRACT LAW COMMITTEE MINUTES

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Katrena Woodson with the Palos Verdes Library District announced upcoming events through
the Library that will be happening this summer, including the Picnic on the Peninsula Saturday,
June 7.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  MCGOWAN CONSULTING LLC, PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT (PSA)
  FOR MS4 PERMIT CONSULTING SERVICES FOR THREE FISCAL YEARS (2025-
  28)

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve a new three-year Professional
  Services Agreement (PSA) with McGowan Consulting LLC for MS4 Permit
  compliance assistance for FYs 2025-28 for a not-to-exceed grand total amount of
  $382,910 ($122,650 in FY 2025-26), all to the satisfaction of the City Attorney.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MAY 27, 2025
   APPROVE A NEW THREE-YEAR PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
  (PSA) WITH MCGOWAN CONSULTING LLC FOR MS4 PERMIT
  COMPLIANCE ASSISTANCE FOR FYS 2025-28 FOR A NOT-TO-EXCEED
  GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $382,910 ($122,650 IN FY 2025-26), ALL TO
  THE SATISFACTION OF THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

B.  TASK ORDER NO. 2025-14 FOR WILLDAN ENGINEERING TO PROVIDE
  ENGINEERING DESIGN SERVICES AND GRANT FUNDING ADMINISTRATION
  FOR ROADWAY GUARDRAIL UPGRADES (CITY-WIDE) UNDER THE CALTRANS
  HIGHWAY SAFETY IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM (HSIP), CYCLE 11 GRANT
  PROGRAM

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve Task Order Number 2025-14 under
  Willdan Engineering’s Master Professional Services Agreement, in the amount of
  $57,154, all to the satisfaction of the City Attorney

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE TASK ORDER NUMBER 2025-14 UNDER WILLDAN
  ENGINEERING’S MASTER PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT, IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $57,154, ALL TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE CITY
  ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

C.  ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB ESTATES HOMEOWNERS ASSOCIATION
  LICENSE AGREEMENT FOR PRIVATE SECURITY CAMERA EQUIPMENT
  LOCATED ON CITY PROPERTY

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Rolling Hills Country Club
  Estates Homeowners Association License Agreement for Private Security Camera
  Equipment Located on City Property which will allow neighborhood cameras to be
  installed on City rights-of-way.

Assistant to the City Manager Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Assistant to the City Manager Slawson confirmed that the Homeowners Association has
applied and qualified for the camera grant program, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER
HUFF.

Assistant City Attorney McEwen made note of a Scribner’s error in the contract attached to
the staff report, in section III “Term” should reference section 14 not 16, which will be
corrected before execution.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE AS AMENDED, THE ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB ESTATES
  HOMEOWNERS ASSOCIATION LICENSE AGREEMENT FOR PRIVATE
  SECURITY CAMERA EQUIPMENT LOCATED ON CITY PROPERTY WHICH

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MAY 27, 2025
   WILL ALLOW NEIGHBORHOOD CAMERAS TO BE INSTALLED ON CITY
  RIGHTS-OF-WAY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

D.  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM: LETTER OF SUPPORT
  FOR SOUTH COAST AIR QUALITY MANAGEMENT DISTRICT (SCAQMD)
  PROPOSED AMENDED RULES (PAR) 1111 AND 1121 - TO REQUIRE ZERO-
  EMISSION STANDARDS FOR RESIDENTIAL FURNACES AND WATER HEATERS

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the Mayor to sign the letter of
  support to Proposed Amended Rules 1111 (Reduction of NOx Emissions from natural
  Gas-Fired Furnaces) and 1121 (Reduction of NOx Emissions from Residential Type,
  Natural Gas-Fired Water Heaters).

Community Development Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

MAYOR STEGURA, as Chair of the Environmental Advisory Committee, explained the split 4-
2 vote by the Committee. She expressed concern about the financial burden that would be put
onto residents, the increase burden on the electrical grid, the rebates that will not likely go to
the Rolling Hills Estates community. She stated she believes it is not the right time to take a
stance on this proposal and that the City should take a no position on this issue.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ expressed concern about targeting a single energy source.

COUNCIL MEMBERS HUFF and SCHACHTER echoed the concerns of the Council related
to the electrical grid and impact on residents.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
Public testimony was received from Gary Tavetian on behalf of the Sierra Club in support of
the letter.

Discussion ended when no motion was moved.

  NO ACTION TAKEN.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 751 ADOPTING
  UPDATED HAZARD SEVERITY ZONES AS RECOMMENDED BY THE CALIFORNIA
  DEPARTMENT OF FORESTRY AND FIRE PROTECTION PURSUANT TO
  GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 51178

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Take public testimony; 2) Discuss
  Ordinance No. 751; 3) Close the public hearing; 4) Conduct the second reading and
  adopt Ordinance No. 751.

Assistant to the City Manager Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

Discussion ensued about the importance of staying vigilant about wildfire risks regardless of
changes to the maps.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MAY 27, 2025
   COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  CONDUCT SECOND READING AND ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 751.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance No. 751 by title.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.
11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ attended the Rotary Club of Palos Verdes Peninsula’s
Responders Roundup event on Saturday, May 17, 2025.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF attended the California Contract Cities Association’s (CCCA)
Annual Municipal Seminar last week along with City Manager Grammer and today attended
the California Association of Councils of Governments (CalCOG) Legislative Day in
Sacramento.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER attended the Traffic and Safety Committee meeting last
week.

MAYOR STEGURA spoke at the Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber of Commerce’s State of
the Peninsula Breakfast, attended the Peninsula Mayor’s Lunch and Los Angeles County
Sanitation District Board meeting last week, participated in the South Bay Cities Council of
Governments (SBCCOG) subcommittee meeting exploring a housing trust for the region,
chaired the Environmental Advisory Committee meeting, and attended the annual Memorial
Day celebration at Green Hills Memorial.

MAYOR SCHMITZ also reminded the community about the Wildfire Preparedness Meeting
tomorrow night at South Coast Botanic Garden at 5:30 pm sponsored by Supervisor Janice
Hahn’s office.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

None.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

None.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:14 p.m. MAYOR STEGURA adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, June 3, 2025, at 5:00
p.m. for the purpose of a Budget Study Session.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit, City Clerk  Debby Stegura, Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MAY 27, 2025
